verses.text: A man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was blameless and upright, revered God, and turned away from evil.
He had seven sons and three daughters.

He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred teams of oxen, and five hundred female donkeys. He had a very large household and was the most prominent man among all the people of the east.
Each of his sons held a feast at his own house on his birthday. They invited their three sisters to eat and drink with them.

When the days of feasting were over, Job would send for his children and consecrate them. He'd get up early and present a burnt offering for each one. He thought, "Maybe my children have sinned and turned against God in their hearts." Job made a practice of this.
One day the sons of God came to present themselves before the LORD, and Satan came with them.
The LORD asked Satan, "Where have you come from?" Satan replied, "From roaming back and forth across the earth and walking all over it."
The LORD asked Satan, "Have you paid attention to my servant Job? There's no one like him on earth. He's blameless and upright, reveres God, and turns away from evil."
Satan answered, "Does Job fear God for nothing?
Haven't you put a hedge around him, his household, and everything he owns? You've blessed his work, and his possessions have spread across the land.
Reach out and strike everything he owns, and he'll turn against you to your face."
The LORD told Satan, "Everything he owns is in your power. Keep your hand off Job himself." Then Satan left the LORD's presence.
One day Job's sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother's house.
A messenger came to Job and said, "The oxen were plowing and the donkeys were grazing beside them
when the Sabeans attacked and took them. They killed the servants with the sword. I'm the only one who escaped to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another messenger came and said, "The fire of God fell from the sky and burned up the sheep and the servants. I'm the only one who escaped to tell you."

While he was still speaking, another came and said, "The Chaldeans divided into three groups, swept down on the camels, and took them. They killed the servants with the sword. I'm the only one who escaped to tell you."
While he was still speaking, another came and said, "Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine at their oldest brother's house.
Suddenly a powerful wind came from the wilderness and struck all four corners of the house. It collapsed on them, and they're dead. I'm the only one who escaped to tell you."
Job stood up, tore his robe, and shaved his head. Then he fell to the ground and worshiped.
He said, "I came naked from my mother's womb, and I'll leave this life naked. The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away. May the LORD's name be blessed."
Through all of this Job neither sinned nor accused God of wrongdoing.
